region.text: the Duchy of Burgundy

ledger.note: 1363: Philip the Bold receives the Duchy of Burgundy in apanage and the Burgundian State begins. 'in 1363, he returned this duchy to the crown to receive instead the Duchy of Burgundy in apanage from his father'; infobox reign from 6 September 1363. The Burgundian State page gives 'Appointed duke of Burgundy in 1363' and a formal recognition on 2 June 1364; the Crown lands page puts the apanage in 1364.

region.text: the County of Flanders; the County of Artois

ledger.note: 30 January 1384: Louis II of Flanders dies and Philip the Bold becomes count consort of Flanders and Artois. Page: 'Count consort of Flanders, Artois, Rethel, Nevers and Burgundy' after Louis II died on 30 January 1384. The Philip the Bold page says Margaret 'in 1382 inherited the County of Flanders, the Duchy of Brabant, the County of Artois, and the Free County of Burgundy' (1369 marriage on 19 June); the pages disagree on the year and on Brabant.

region.text: the Free County of Burgundy

ledger.note: 1384: the Free County of Burgundy (Franche-Comté) joins Flanders and Artois under Philip the Bold, as Margaret's inheritance. Same page sentence ('... Artois, Rethel, Nevers and Burgundy').

region.text: the County of Nevers; the County of Rethel

ledger.note: 1384: Nevers and Rethel come with Margaret's inheritance (joint rule with Margaret, 1384). The department of Ardennes is my reading of Rethel.

region.text: the counties of Nevers and Rethel

ledger.note: 1407: Nevers and Rethel pass to Philip II of Nevers, Philip the Bold's younger son. Philip II, Count of Nevers page (opened 2026-11-01): infobox 'Count of Nevers 1404-1415' and 'Count of Rethel 1406-1415', 'succeeded his brothers' after each acceded to his duchy; County of Nevers page: 'Philip's younger son Philip II was granted the County of Nevers'. Mirror of county-of-nevers ledger/12 (1407 gain, counterpart duchy-of-burgundy) and duchy-of-burgundy ledger/14. The page dates the titles 1404 and 1406; 1407 is Cliopatria's split year, kept so the three dossiers agree. The department of Ardennes is the reading of Rethel used in the 1384 gain. [fx-30 2026-11-01, finding F251: added; the dossier had no loss and drew the counties as Burgundian to 1482.]

region.text: the County of Namur

ledger.note: 1429: Philip the Good incorporates Namur. Page: 'In 1429, he incorporated Namur into Burgundian territory' (bought from John III, Marquis of Namur); the Burgundian State page says he bought it in 1421 and inherited it outright in 1429.

region.text: the Duchy of Brabant (Limburg is not drawn separately)

ledger.note: 1430: Philip the Good inherits Brabant and Limburg from his cousin Philip of Saint-Pol. Page: 'He inherited the Duchies of Brabant and Limburg'. The Burgundian State page adds Luxembourg in 1430 and then dates its purchase to 1441.

region.text: the County of Hainaut; the County of Holland; Zeeland; Friesland

ledger.note: 1432: Philip the Good takes Hainaut, Holland, Friesland and Zeeland from Jacqueline. Page: 'Hainault and Holland, Friesland and Zeeland in 1432 with the defeat of Jacqueline'. The Burgundian State page dates it to her death in 1433 ('at the time of her death, in 1433, he seized her Counties of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland').

union.text: the Somme towns and Péronne, Ponthieu

region.text: the Somme towns and Péronne, Ponthieu; Vermandois, with its capital Saint-Quentin; the County of Auxerre; the County of Boulogne

ledger.note: 20/21 September 1435: the Treaty of Arras gives Philip the Somme towns, Vermandois, Auxerre, Boulogne and Ponthieu. Page: the County of Auxerre and the County of Boulogne, 'the Somme towns and Péronne', Ponthieu, and Vermandois 'with its capital Saint-Quentin' became vassal domains of the Duke of Burgundy; Burgundy recognized Charles VII and returned the County of Tonnerre. The page gives no redemption terms.

region.text: the Duchy of Luxembourg

ledger.note: 1443: Philip the Good buys Luxembourg. Page: Philip 'purchased Luxembourg in 1443' from Elisabeth of Bohemia; the Burgundian State page says 1441 'he bought from his aunt Elizabeth of Görlitz'.

region.text: the Somme towns and Péronne, Ponthieu

ledger.note: 1463: Philip gives up some land to Louis XI. Page: Philip 'gave up some of his territory to King Louis XI of France' (no details). The page is silent on which land; the Somme towns of the 1435 Arras gains are my reading and the reviewer should treat this as a gap.

region.text: Sigismund's Upper Alsace lands (Sundgau and Breisgau), bought in 1469

ledger.note: 1469: Charles the Bold buys Upper Alsace from Sigismund of Austria. Burgundian State page: 'after the 1469 purchase of Brisgau and Sundgau'; Charles the Bold page: on 21 March 1469 Charles received Sigismund 'to negotiate the purchase of Sigismund's Upper Alsace lands'. It was a pledge, not a sovereign cession; the region Alsace is my reading of Sundgau.

region.text: 'effectively turning the duchy into a Burgundian protectorate'

ledger.note: 1473: Charles the Bold makes Lorraine a Burgundian protectorate. Page: through René II, Charles 'gained the right to move armies through Lorraine, effectively turning the duchy into a Burgundian protectorate'.

region.text: the Duchy of Guelders

ledger.note: 1473: Guelders comes to Charles the Bold. Page: in February 1473 Arnold of Guelders died and bequeathed the duchy to Charles; on 9 June 1473 Charles entered Maastricht, and Roermond and Venlo 'quickly surrendered' and Nijmegen 'only after heavy losses'. Zutphen is not reported as taken.

region.text: Sigismund's Upper Alsace lands (Sundgau and Breisgau), bought in 1469

ledger.note: April 1474: Upper Alsace rises against Burgundian rule and the pledged lands are lost. Charles the Bold page: 'In April 1474, rebellion broke out in Alsace, and the league declared war on Burgundy in support of the rebels.' The page does not describe the redemption itself; the house-of-habsburg dossier ends its Burgundian pawn of Alsace in 1474. [Reviewer eu-10-x, 2026-10-25] moved from 5 January 1477 (confidence 1) to the page's April 1474.

region.text: 'Finally, in 1475, he conquered the Duchy of Lorraine'

ledger.note: 1475: the protectorate ends in conquest. Page: 'Finally, in 1475, he conquered the Duchy of Lorraine'.

region.text: the Duchy of Lorraine

ledger.note: 1475: Charles the Bold conquers the Duchy of Lorraine. Page: 'Finally, in 1475, he conquered the Duchy of Lorraine'; the Charles the Bold page has him capture Nancy after the 1475 peace and before the siege of Grandson, without a date.

region.text: the Duchy of Lorraine

ledger.note: 6 October 1476: René II retakes Nancy and Lorraine is lost. Burgundian State page: 'In 1476 the Duke of Lorraine retook Nancy'; Charles the Bold page: 'Nancy was reconquered by René II on 6 October' (year implied by context).

region.text: 'invaded Burgundian territory through Picardy, Artois, and Mâcon'

ledger.note: January 1477: Louis XI invades the Burgundian lands after Charles's death. Charles the Bold page: Charles 'was killed at the Battle of Nancy on 5 January 1477'; about three weeks later Louis XI 'invaded Burgundian territory through Picardy, Artois, and Mâcon'. The page does not say he seized Burgundy; the zone is Picardy, Artois and the duchy.

region.text: the Second Treaty of Arras

ledger.note: 23 December 1482: the Second Treaty of Arras ends the war of succession. Infobox: Mary's death 27 March 1482; Second Treaty of Arras 23 December 1482; 'signed on December 1482'.

union.text: the Somme towns and Péronne, Ponthieu

region.text: the Duchy of Burgundy; the Somme towns and Péronne, Ponthieu; Vermandois, with its capital Saint-Quentin; the County of Auxerre; the County of Boulogne; the County of Artois; the Free County of Burgundy

ledger.note: December 1482: Burgundy and Picardy pass to France. Page: the treaty gave 'Burgundy's dukedom and Picardy' to France 'and the Netherlands stayed with the Habsburgs'; 'By the Treaty of Senlis of 1493, the French king gave back Artois, Charolais and the County of Burgundy', so France held Artois and the Free County from 1482 to 1493. [fx-30 2026-11-01, finding F251: Nevers and Rethel removed from the region: they were Philip II of Nevers's line's from 1407 (Philip II page, county-of-nevers ledger/12), not the Burgundian state's to lose.]

region.text: the dukedom and Picardy to France; the Netherlands to the Habsburgs

ledger.note: December 1482: the Burgundian State ends; the dukedom goes to France and the Netherlands to the Habsburgs. Page: after Mary's death 'the Burgundian lands were divided'; 'the Burgundian Netherlands passed to the Spanish Empire of King Philip II' after Charles V's abdication in 1555.

wars.name: Hundred Years' War (Burgundian phase)

zones.text: the Somme towns and Picardy gained at Arras

wars.outcome: The Treaty of Arras (20/21 September 1435) revoked the Treaty of Troyes, made Philip recognize Charles VII and gave him the Somme towns, Vermandois, Auxerre, Boulogne and Ponthieu.
wars.note: Burgundian control of Paris from May 1418 is in the royal-domain-of-france dossier (Treaty of Troyes page).

wars.name: Burgundian Wars
wars.outcome: Charles conquered Lorraine in 1475, lost Nancy to René II on 6 October 1476 and was killed at Nancy on 5 January 1477.
wars.note: The Swiss defeats at Grandson (March 1476) and Morat (22 June 1476) are in the Charles page; no territory changed at either.

wars.name: War of the Burgundian Succession
wars.outcome: Louis XI overran Picardy, Artois and the duchy after Nancy; the Second Treaty of Arras (23 December 1482) gave Burgundy and Picardy to France and left the Netherlands to the Habsburgs.
wars.note: The war article was not opened (page budget); dates are the Burgundian State page's infobox.

certainty.note: A composite of feudal counties and duchies with no boundary survey; the Arras lines of 1435 and 1482 are treaty lines and the Netherlands/France frontier follows the counties.

notes:
Written for eu-10-x from five pages (Burgundian State, Philip the Bold, Philip the Good, Charles the Bold, Treaty of Arras 1435). None gives an area, so no infobox comparison was possible. The brief's scope says 'the Burgundian state 1363 to 1477'; the page's infobox runs to the Second Treaty of Arras (23 December 1482) and Mary of Burgundy ruled the Netherlands and the French-held rest until her death on 27 March 1482, so the state ends in December 1482 and 1477-1482 is a contest zone (Picardy, Artois, the duchy), not an end.
OVERLAPS: Cliopatria has the Duchy of Burgundy 1003-1481 (eu-10-d or similar group), the County of Flanders to 1384, Brabant to 1430, Holland to 1362, Luxembourg 1429-1449 and the Free County of Burgundy 1333-1384 as separate rows. This dossier is the composite layer and its keyframes are generated from its gains and losses; the compile must draw it over those rows (or let this one win where both exist), as for the royal domain.
PAGES DISAGREE: Hainaut/Holland/Zeeland 1432 (Philip the Good) or 1433 (Burgundian State); Luxembourg 1443 (Philip the Good) or 1441 (Burgundian State); Namur 1429 or 1421 bought and 1429 inherited; Flanders 1384 (Burgundian State) or 1382 (Philip the Bold); the Duchy of Burgundy apanage 1363 (Philip the Bold, Burgundian State) or 1364 (Crown lands page). The year of each event is the cited page's.
NOT DRAWN: Limburg (1430, no separate region; inside the Brabant text), Charolais (1390, within or beside the duchy), Mechelen and Antwerp, the Tonnerre return (1435), Zutphen (1473, not reported taken), Franche-Comté lost 1482-1493 beyond the loss event. Guelders is never shown lost: the pages opened say nothing on its loss after Charles's death (a gap for the reviewer).
CONF 1: the 1463 loss (the page names no land) and (the 1477 Alsace loss was moved to April 1474 at confidence 2 by reviewer eu-10-x, from the Charles the Bold page).
Counterparts without a Cliopatria row or dossier: County of Namur, Duchy of Guelders, County of Hainaut (listed in the report).
